model.rationale: Fletcher pairs incumbency in a D+13 Houston-area seat with a lopsided money advantage over an underfunded challenger, and prediction markets price her near-certain; with no polls or ratings signaling risk, the race stays comfortably in Safe D territory.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Fletcher or an unexpected poll showing a single-digit contest would warrant a downgrade.

overview:
TX-07 covers western Houston and leans Democratic by about 13 points on the partisan index. Lizzie Fletcher, first elected in 2018, is seeking another term with the advantages of incumbency in a district that has trended her party's way. Her Republican challenger, Alexander Hale, has run a minimal campaign, reporting roughly $77,000 raised and about $6,000 on hand, with no outside spending reported on either side. A Green Party candidate is also on the ballot with negligible funding.

Fletcher has raised about $1.4 million and holds $1.7 million in cash, giving her a dominant advertising and organization edge. Prediction markets put her chances around 96 percent. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district lean, incumbency, and money, all pointing to a comfortable Democratic win.
